chunks: What the Sheikh (may Allah the Exalted support him) informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara, from 'Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may the blessings of Allah be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said to me: 'When you enter the toilet, do not face the qibla and do not turn your back to it; rather, face east or west.'

key_terms.اَلْقِبْلَةَ: al-qibla: the prayer direction toward the Kaʿba in Mecca
key_terms.اَلْمَخْرَجَ: al-makhraj: the lavatory, place of relieving oneself
key_terms.تَسْتَدْبِرْهَا: to turn one's back to (the qibla)
key_terms.تَسْتَقْبِلِ: to face toward, orient oneself in the direction of
key_terms.شَرِّقُوا: face east, orient toward the east

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (SAWW) instruct Imam Ali (AS) about facing the qibla direction when entering the toilet?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) personally directed Imam Ali (AS) that upon entering al-makhraj (the lavatory), one must neither face the qibla nor turn one's back to it, but orient oneself east or west instead. This ruling establishes a jurisprudential prohibition protecting the sanctity of the qibla direction during the act of relieving oneself — a ruling found across both Sunni and Shia fiqh traditions, with this Shia chain tracing directly to a private prophetic instruction to Imam Ali (AS).
